children: California utility PG&E will slash its planned spending by $2 billion next year and launch a review of its business after a state legislative debate over wildfire liabilities was left unresolved.

Shares fell nearly 10%, putting PG&E stock on track for its lowest close since 2022. Chief Executive Patti Poppe said the company faces a "fundamental challenge" of a wildfire liability framework that has effectively stranded the utility in sub-investment grade territory, which has led to higher borrowing costs that are passed to customers.
The company's planned capital spending next year will drop to $11.4 billion from $13.4 billion, it said Wednesday.

"We believe that we could do better for customers if we could continue to invest and transform the business at the pace that we have been, but we can't," Poppe said in an interview. "Our customers can't afford us to do that, and so that's why we're just really putting the stake in the ground that something must change."
The utility will continue safety-related work, but delay some projects tied to economic development that have more "flexibility in timing," she said.
California Gov. Gavin Newsom and lawmakers were at odds over his preferred reforms, which included reducing investor-owned utilities' wildfire liabilities.
